key_insight: WorldSolver shows that LLM agents can sometimes generate physics simulators, but reliably producing executable, visually accurate, and physically plausible solvers remains very difficult.
engineering_relevance: The benchmark targets a core engineering bottleneck in simulation workflows: turning physical understanding into executable solver code for dynamic systems.
method: 168 simulation tasks derived from 61 classic computer graphics papers
Covers 7 physical domains with fixed code scaffolds and missing solver logic
Evaluates agents on execution success, visual fidelity, and physical plausibility
evidence_signal: Across frontier agents, execution alone is challenging, and the best reported overall scores are only 48.7% for GPT-5.6-Sol and 46.7% for Claude-Opus-5.
watch_item: A solver that runs successfully may still produce visually convincing but physically incorrect dynamics, so deployment should include physics-grounded verification beyond code execution.
paper_title: WorldSolver: Can LLM Agents Simulate the Physical Dynamics via Solver Generation?
